description: NestJS HTTP controllers: which decorators make a class a controller, a method a route, and a route versioned.

rules.description: A class decorated @Controller(path) serves the routes its methods declare with @Get, @Post, @Put, @Patch, @Delete, @Options, @Head and @All, each under the controller's path, when a module decorated @Module lists it among its controllers. @Version on a method, or on the controller or in its options, names the route's version: one, a list of them, or VERSION_NEUTRAL for none.
rules.why: These are @nestjs/common's own decorators. The application is the one NestFactory.create makes and then listens on; its setGlobalPrefix puts a prefix before every route, and enableVersioning with VersioningType.URI puts the version (v1, the prefix Nest adds by default) after that prefix; a route with no version of its own takes the controller's, then the defaultVersion. A module RouterModule.register names a path serves its controllers under that path. The bridge reads those calls from the bootstrap and the controllers each module registers; the examples here read what one class declares.

examples.why: a path variable is written {id}, as every other lane writes one, so a frontend call matches it
a list of versions serves the route under each, and VERSION_NEUTRAL on the method serves it under none, whatever the controller says
a path held in a variable is not read here, and the bridge makes no route of it
a method decorator serves nothing on a class that is not a controller
